title: O, TWINE ME A BOWER or BLUE EYES AND GOLDEN HAIR or THE GROVES OF BLARNEY
html_source:
These songs of ideal love, beauty, and setting are among the first signs of Stephen’s increasing awareness of the blemishes of reality in contrast to the perfections supposed in his innocence. The beauty of the songs can hardly be fully appreciated with Stephen now painfully cognizant of “the reeking outhouse” which provides the incongrous setting for their execution. – Zack R. Bowen, Musical Allusions in the Works of James Joyce
